_comment: Cross-runtime oracle for reading a stored strategy_analytics row as DAILY RETURNS (Phase 164.6.6.2.2 D-01, D-02). `returns_series` is the cumulative CURVE (wealth levels), not returns; `daily_returns`, when non-empty, wins. Read by tests/test_wealth_returns.py and, from plan 164.6.6.2.2-03, by src/lib/factsheet/resolve-series.test.ts. Every `expected` value is a HAND-COMPUTED literal (see each `arithmetic`), never produced by either implementation. A JSON `null` curve value stands for a non-finite level (JSON has no NaN). Day 0 never emits; a day whose stored-adjacent level pair is unusable is ABSENT from `expected` (never 0, never bridged across the bad level). Geometric: r_k = w_k / w_{k-1} - 1 on two finite levels > 0. Simple: r_k = w_k - w_{k-1} on two finite levels.

cases.name: geometric_ratio
cases.arithmetic: Geometric (flags absent reads geometric). d1 = 1.1 / 1.0 - 1 = 0.1; d2 = 1.21 / 1.1 - 1 = 0.1. Day 0 (2026-03-02) has no prior level and is dropped.

cases.name: simple_difference
cases.arithmetic: Simple (flags cumulative_method = simple). d1 = 1.1 - 1.0 = 0.1; d2 = 1.15 - 1.1 = 0.05. The geometric ratio would give 0.0454545... for d2.

cases.name: same_curve_simple_reads_a_difference
cases.arithmetic: Same curve 1.0, 1.1, 1.2 read SIMPLE: d1 = 1.1 - 1.0 = 0.1; d2 = 1.2 - 1.1 = 0.1. The two methods differ on d2 (1/11 vs 0.1).

cases.name: nonpositive_level_mid_series
cases.arithmetic: Geometric levels 1.0, 1.1, 0, 1.2, 1.32. d1 = 1.1 / 1.0 - 1 = 0.1. d2 pairs 0 with 1.1 and d3 pairs 1.2 with 0: a level of 0 is not > 0, so both days are ABSENT (never 0, never bridged as 1.2 / 1.1 - 1). d4 = 1.32 / 1.2 - 1 = 0.1.

cases.name: nonpositive_level_is_legal_on_simple
cases.arithmetic: Simple levels 1.0, 0.5, -0.1, 0.2 (a non-positive level is legal on a running-sum curve). d1 = 0.5 - 1.0 = -0.5; d2 = -0.1 - 0.5 = -0.6; d3 = 0.2 - (-0.1) = 0.3.

cases.name: non_finite_level_drops_dependent_days
cases.arithmetic: Geometric levels 1.0, 1.1, null, 1.3, 1.43 (a JSON null is a non-finite level). d1 = 1.1 / 1.0 - 1 = 0.1. d2 and d3 pair with the null level and are ABSENT (d3 is not bridged as 1.3 / 1.1 - 1). d4 = 1.43 / 1.3 - 1 = 0.1.

cases.name: non_finite_level_drops_dependent_days_simple
cases.arithmetic: Simple levels 1.0, 1.1, null, 1.3, 1.4. d1 = 1.1 - 1.0 = 0.1. d2 and d3 pair with the null level and are ABSENT (d3 is not bridged as 1.3 - 1.1 = 0.2). d4 = 1.4 - 1.3 = 0.1.

cases.name: daily_returns_first_wins
cases.arithmetic: A non-empty daily_returns is returned verbatim (0.03, -0.02) and the curve (which would read 0.1, 0.1) is ignored.

cases.name: daily_returns_empty_list_falls_to_curve
cases.arithmetic: daily_returns = [] is empty, so the curve is read geometric: d1 = 1.1 / 1.0 - 1 = 0.1; d2 = 1.21 / 1.1 - 1 = 0.1.

cases.name: daily_returns_empty_dict_falls_to_curve
cases.arithmetic: daily_returns = {} is empty, so the curve is read geometric: d1 = 0.1; d2 = 0.1.

cases.name: daily_returns_without_a_finite_value_falls_to_curve
cases.arithmetic: daily_returns holds one record whose value is null (non-finite), so it carries no usable value and the curve is read geometric: d1 = 0.1; d2 = 0.1.

cases.name: daily_returns_flat_dict_shape
cases.arithmetic: Flat {date: value} daily_returns {2026-03-03: 0.03, 2026-03-04: -0.02} is read verbatim; the curve is ignored.

cases.name: daily_returns_nested_dict_shape_zero_pads
cases.arithmetic: Nested {year: {M-D: value}} daily_returns {2026: {3-3: 0.03, 03-04: -0.02}}: the short key 3-3 is zero-padded to 03-03, so the dates are 2026-03-03 and 2026-03-04 with the verbatim values.

cases.name: unsorted_input_is_sorted
cases.arithmetic: The curve arrives as 1.21 (03-04), 1.0 (03-02), 1.1 (03-03) and is sorted by date before pairing: d1 = 1.1 / 1.0 - 1 = 0.1; d2 = 1.21 / 1.1 - 1 = 0.1.

cases.name: zero_point_series_is_empty
cases.arithmetic: No stored point: no day is formable, the result is empty.

cases.name: one_point_series_is_empty
cases.arithmetic: One stored point has no predecessor: day 0 never emits, the result is empty.

cases.name: unknown_method_string_reads_geometric
cases.arithmetic: cumulative_method = arithmetic is not a recognised literal, so the curve reads geometric: d1 = 0.1; d2 = 1.2 / 1.1 - 1 = 1/11 = 0.0909090909090909... (simple would give 0.1).

cases.name: absent_method_key_reads_geometric
cases.arithmetic: data_quality_flags carries no cumulative_method, so the curve reads geometric: d1 = 0.1; d2 = 1.2 / 1.1 - 1 = 1/11 = 0.0909090909090909...

cases.name: native_leg_loses_first_two_days
cases.arithmetic: Geometric curve 1.0, 1.1, 1.21, 1.331 on 03-02..03-05 gives native returns 0.1 on 03-03, 03-04 and 03-05 (day 0 dropped by the curve read). The BTC conversion then drops the first remaining day (03-03 has no prior priced day) and prices the rest: usd = (1 + r) * (close_k / close_{k-1}) - 1 with closes 100 (03-03), 110 (03-04), 99 (03-05). 03-04: 1.1 * (110 / 100) - 1 = 1.21 - 1 = 0.21. 03-05: 1.1 * (99 / 110) - 1 = 1.1 * 0.9 - 1 = -0.01. Only the days from the curve's day 2 on survive.
